standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the right-hand side: maps of complexes from the tensor product correspond to graded bilinear maps compatible with differentials, the target description of the adjunction.

standard_prerequisites.name: Maps out of a total tensor product
standard_prerequisites.use: Determines, from an element of the left-hand side, the map of complexes out of the total tensor product, the starting point of the translation.

core_obligations: The common description (proof lines 1896-1901): both sides correspond to graded A-bilinear maps M x M' to N compatible with differentials; the right-hand side identification is the one fixed in the tensor-product section.

From the adjoint to the bilinear map (proof lines 1902-1912): an element g of the left-hand side determines via more-algebra-lemma-compose a map of complexes g' out of the total of M' tensor_R M; precomposing with the commutativity constraint gives a map out of the total of M tensor_R M', hence a graded R-bilinear map g'' compatible with differentials.

The A-linearity sign computation (proof lines 1913-1937): writing out g''(x, ax') and g''(xa, x') for x in degree e, x' in degree e' and a in degree n, the two displayed expansions differ only by sign exponents, and the parity check on the exponents shows they agree, so A-linearity of g translates into A-bilinearity of g''.
proof_roadmap: State the bilinear description both sides share.
Translate a left-hand-side element through the compose lemma and the commutativity constraint into a bilinear map.
Verify the A-bilinearity by the explicit sign computation on the two orders of the action.
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the hom-tensor adjunction between right and left differential graded modules and complexes of R-modules (statement lines 1884-1895). The proof (lines 1897-1937) runs through a common bilinear description: the translation of an adjoint map into a bilinear map via the compose lemma and the commutativity constraint, and then a genuine sign computation verifying that A-linearity transfers, with both displayed expansions closed by a parity check on the exponents. H2: the sign bookkeeping is the content; each ingredient is standard but the degree-shifted A-action signs must be tracked exactly and are computed in the span.
